newsitem.title: USA: All American sees Q4 sales of $57 million.
newsitem.headline: All American sees Q4 sales of $57 million.

text.p: All American Semiconductor Inc Wednesday said unaudited sales for the fourth quarter topped $57 million, a rise of about 15 percent over sales of $50 million for the year-ago period.

The distributor of electronic components also said it expects to take a non-cash, non-recurring charge in the fourth quarter of about $625,000. The charge is for the acceleration of an existing accrual schedule in connection with the post-retirement benefits contained in an employment agreement with an executive officer of the company.

The need to accelerate the accrual schedule arose from an amendment to his employment agreement where, in exchange for a voluntary reduction in salary and a release of certain insurance obligations of the company, the executive was granted the right to retire at any time and begin receiving post-retirement benefits, which are substantially less than his present compensation package.
Company officials were not available for details.

In a statement, the company also said unaudited 1996 sales were in excess of $244 million, an increase of about 35 percent over sales of $181 million in 1995. These sales amounts include revenues from discontinued operations.

Bruce Goldberg, president and chief operating officer of All American, said the improved 1996 results reflected sales from acquired companies as well as continued market share improvement, new office openings and more product offerings.

"While we are disappointed with our results through the first nine months of 1996, we are encouraged by the positive impact of our restructurings and the progress of the cost control programs we put in place. We expect that our fourth quarter results will be back to an operating profit before interest, taxes and any non-cash, non-recurring charges."
